jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
About GHOSTGOLF

GHOSTGOLF is a premium golf equipment, accessories, bags, and apparel brand on an aggressive growth trajectory. We sell across three channels simultaneously — direct-to-consumer, wholesale through pro shops and golf boutiques, and big box retail through Dick's Sporting Goods, Golf Galaxy, PGA Tour Super Store, Scheels and others. We also operate a corporate retail store.
We move fast, operate lean, and build things that last. Our products are premium. Our standards are high. Our team is getting bigger.
We are looking for an operator who has been in the trenches. Someone who has scaled a consumer goods or apparel brand, built systems where none existed, and knows the difference between a plan on paper and one that actually executes under pressure.

The Role

This role is structured as Director of Operations.
You will own everything that keeps this business running and growing — operations, systems, logistics, inventory, fulfillment, retail, and the people who execute across all of it. You work directly with the founder and report to no one else.
This is not a manage-and-maintain role. We are mid-build. There are warehouses being transitioned, an ERP being implemented, a retail store being scaled, a team being built, and three sales channels that need to operate in sync. You are the person who makes all of that happen on time and without breaking what is working.
In 90 days, you will have taken ownership of our warehouse operations, led our ERP implementation through go-live, established clean sales operations across all three channels, and built the hiring plan for the next twelve months.
In twelve months, you will have built the operational infrastructure that gets Ghost Golf to 2X current revenue and beyond.

What You'll Own

Warehouse Operations
— Own the day-to-day management of warehouse and fulfillment operations. Lead the full build-out and transition of our new Irvine facility — warehouse layout, rack plan, bin locations, pick path design, and scanning infrastructure. Implement RFID compliance across 100% of our product catalog by December 31, 2026 — a hard, non-negotiable deadline required by our retail partners. Evaluate and select a WMS that handles DTC, wholesale, and retail order flows from a single platform. Manage inbound freight, receiving operations, and carrier relationships. Own returns and reverse logistics. Build and lead the warehouse team from the ground up at the new facility. Establish performance metrics including units per hour, order accuracy, fulfillment SLAs, and cost per order.
Corporate Retail Store
— Own the full build-out and ongoing operations of our new corporate retail location at our Irvine headquarters. Partner with architects and fabricators on store design, fixture selection, and physical build-out from conception through opening day. Implement and configure our POS system. Hire, schedule, and lead a team of retail associates running 7 days a week, 11 AM – 6 PM. Establish daily store operations — inventory allocation, visual merchandising standards, replenishment, and brand standards. Ensure the store operates in full sync with our DTC and wholesale channels — consistent pricing, product availability, and a brand experience that reflects Ghost Golf at its best.
Systems and Technology
— Lead ERP implementation from selection through go-live. We are evaluating multiple ERPs at this time. The selected ERP must integrate cleanly with Shopify, QuickBooks, and our B2B platforms — and must support or include WMS functionality to reduce system complexity. Own the full systems stack — ERP, WMS, and CRM. Ensure RFID readiness is built into the systems architecture from day one.
Inventory and Production Planning — Own demand forecasting, purchase order management, and inventory positioning across DTC, wholesale, and retail. Build the planning process from the ground up. Eliminate stockouts. Reduce overstock. Ensure retail ship windows are met and chargebacks are driven to zero.
Sales Operations
— Support the sales team across all three channels. Own CRM hygiene and reporting. Manage EDI compliance with major retail partners. Build the operational infrastructure that allows the wholesale and big box businesses to scale without adding headcount.
Finance and Reporting — P&L ownership in partnership with the founder. Weekly operational reporting. Budget management. Cost discipline across all operational functions.
Team Building
— We are moving from founder-led to structured. You build the team. You hire, develop, and lead. You establish the culture and the standards of the operations function.

What We're Looking For

Experience

7+ years in operations leadership — Director of Operations, VP of Operations, or COO
Consumer goods, apparel, or accessories industry — you know the product cycle, production timelines, MOQs, and what it means to operate a physical goods business at scale
Proven ERP implementation experience — you have taken a company through a full implementation and lived to tell about it
Retail store operations experience — corporate or branded retail preferred. You have managed a physical retail location, understand the staffing model, the inventory discipline, and what it takes to run a store that reflects the brand at full volume
DTC, wholesale, and retail operations experience — all three channels, not just one
EDI and retail compliance experience with major retail partners
3PL and logistics management — warehouse buildouts, transitions, and optimization
Team building at scale — you have hired, developed, and led operations teams through a growth phase

Skills

Operations Management
Supply Chain and Logistics
ERP Implementation
DTC Operations
Wholesale and Retail Operations
Retail Store Operations
EDI and Retail Compliance
3PL Management
Financial Planning and Analysis
Team Leadership and Org Building

Character

Bias for action. You build systems where none exist and you do it fast.
High standards. You do not accept mediocre outcomes.
Hands-on. You are not above the work. You are in it.
Clear communicator. You can translate complex operational realities into simple decisions.
Calm under pressure. This business moves fast. You move with it.

What We Offer

Competitive compensation package commensurate with experience
Direct partnership with the founder
The opportunity to build something real from the inside

To Apply

Send your resume and a brief note on why Ghost Golf and why now to hello@ghostgolf.com.

No recruiters.

Job Description Summary

The Managing Director, Advisory Leadership Team serves as a senior leader within the advisory organization, responsible for driving advisor performance, business growth, organizational effectiveness, and the consistent delivery of the Focus Partners client experience. This role serves as a strategic partner to advisors and advisory teams while directly supporting a designated group of advisors in achieving growth, client retention, and business planning objectives.

In addition to advisor leadership responsibilities, the Managing Director partners closely with the Division President to establish divisional priorities, advance strategic initiatives, and support long-term business planning efforts. The role plays a critical part in connecting firm objectives, divisional priorities, and advisor execution by leading key projects, driving organizational improvements, utilizing data-informed decision making, and supporting effective capacity and resource planning across the division.

As a senior member of the division leadership team, the Managing Director serves as a trusted advisor and thought partner to the Division President, helping shape strategy, advance organizational priorities, and drive execution across the division. This role may serve as the Division President's delegate and representative in leadership discussions, cross-functional initiatives, and strategic projects as needed.

Focus provides team members the flexibility to work a hybrid schedule. Our hybrid model is defined as 3 days in office work required per week, while giving team members the option to work remotely 2 days per week, or as assigned by their team leader.

Job Description

Primary Responsibilities

Advisor Leadership & Business Performance

Serve as the primary leadership partner for a designated group of advisors and advisory teams, providing coaching, accountability, and strategic guidance.
Drive advisor growth, client retention, business planning, and overall team performance across assigned practices.
Conduct regular business reviews and performance discussions, leveraging practice metrics and business data to evaluate progress and identify opportunities.
Partner with advisors to strengthen business management, succession planning, team effectiveness, and adoption of the Focus Partners client experience.
Drive the ongoing development of advisor skills, leadership capabilities, and best practices aligned with the Focus Partners client experience framework.
Promote consistency in advisory leadership, business planning, and advisor development practices across the division.

Division Strategy & Organizational Leadership

Partner directly with the Division President to establish divisional objectives, long-term business plans, annual operating goals, and strategic priorities.
Support the development and execution of divisional OKRs and key business initiatives.
Lead strategic projects and organizational initiatives designed to improve advisor effectiveness, increase scalability, and strengthen business performance.
Participate in cross-divisional initiatives and enterprise efforts that advance firm-wide priorities and organizational transformation objectives.
Act as a trusted advisor to the Division President by providing insight regarding advisor trends, leadership opportunities, organizational challenges, and growth initiatives.
Serve as the Division President's delegate and representative in leadership discussions, strategic initiatives, and cross-functional efforts as needed.

Capacity Planning & Operational Excellence

Maintain a disciplined approach to advisor capacity and resource planning, utilizing data and business metrics to support workforce decisions and sustainable growth.
Leverage performance analytics and practice management metrics to monitor results, identify trends, and support data-driven decision making.
Oversee office-level advisory budgets and help ensure resources are effectively aligned with divisional priorities.
Serve as the primary owner of advisor-related business exceptions, including discounting requests, trade errors, and similar matters requiring leadership oversight and resolution.
Partner with Operations, Service, Compliance, Technology, and other business functions to improve advisor effectiveness and enhance client outcomes.
Support the onboarding, integration, and transition of advisors, teams, and firms joining the organization.
Encourage the adoption of technology, tools, processes, and best practices that improve efficiency, consistency, and business results.

Leadership & Culture

Act as a culture ambassador across the advisory community by promoting collaboration, accountability, and alignment with firm values.
Facilitate conflict resolution and help drive productive outcomes across advisors, teams, and business partners.
Collaborate with advisory leaders and other stakeholders to ensure consistency in advisor support and execution of divisional priorities.
Represent the division in leadership forums, Advisory Council activities, and other strategic leadership initiatives.
Support the development of future leaders and contribute to succession planning efforts across the advisory organization.
Foster an inclusive, high-performing environment focused on advisor success and exceptional client outcomes.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required.
CFP®, CFA®, CPA, MBA, or other advanced professional designation preferred.
12+ years of experience within wealth management, financial services, or a related industry.
Significant leadership experience coaching and influencing experienced advisors, leaders, and high-performing teams.
Demonstrated success driving advisor growth, business planning, talent development, and organizational performance.
Proven experience partnering on strategic initiatives, leading cross-functional projects, and successfully executing complex business priorities.
Experience leading through change and contributing to organizational transformation efforts.
Strong understanding of advisory business models, practice management, capacity planning, and resource allocation.
Experience utilizing business metrics, performance reporting, and analytics to support strategic decision making.
Exceptional communication, relationship management, and leadership skills, with the ability to influence across all levels of the organization.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with operational execution in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
Ability to travel approximately 25%.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Development
jobs.description:
POSITION:
Senior Director of Development

ORGANIZATION:
CuriOdyssey ( www.curiodyssey.org )

LOCATION:
San Mateo, California

ORGANIZATION:
CuriOdyssey is a mission-driven, dynamic, family-centric science center and zoo located in Coyote Point Park. Their mission is to inspire a love for science and curiosity about the world.
They have recently completed a strategic reinvention, focusing on a hands-on experiences in concert with the natural world. They have a strong commitment to making science education fully inclusive
, which is integrated into their strategic planning, governance, and daily operations. A core part of this commitment is ensuring access for all, regardless of economic means.
They provide free and low-cost entrance through programs like Museums for All
, Military and Teacher discounts and summer camp scholarships
. They also create an inclusive and welcoming environment through initiatives like Sensory Sundays
and by designing their new facilities, such as the WHOOOSH! playground, to be universally accessible.

Their team includes a dedicated Board of Directors, an energetic staff of 50, and over 70 volunteers. They welcome over 180,000 visitors annually and currently have an annual operating budget of approximately $6 million. The organization is entering an exciting period of growth with opportunities to expand philanthropic investment and community partnerships.

REPORTING RELATIONSHIP:
The Senior Director of Development reports directly to the CEO.

POSITION SUMMARY:
CuriOdyssey is seeking a Senior Director of Development who is excited to inherit a mission-driven, dynamic, family-centric science center and zoo recognized in the community as a leader in early science education.

As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Senior Director of Development serves as a strategic thought partner to the CEO is responsible for the formulation, implementation, and management of all development strategies for the organization. The position supervises 3.5 full time Development team members and works closely with the CEO, the Senior Leadership team, Board of Directors, and community to cultivate relationships with lapsed, current and prospective supporters with the goal of increasing philanthropic support to CuriOdyssey.

The Senior Director oversees CuriOdyssey’s fundraising efforts including annual giving, major gifts, planned giving, corporate and foundation support, sponsorships and special events, as well as a potential capital campaign. The Senior Director of Development oversees these internal functions: Major Gifts Officer, Annual Fund Manager, Development Operations Manager and a contract Grant Writer.

The Senior Director of Development also stewards key external alliances and cultivates philanthropic support. Key metrics for success will include donor engagement through in-person contacts and portfolio development and revenue. The position will create, model, and champion a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.

SCOPE AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Develop and implement a comprehensive and actionable development strategy for major gifts, annual fund, planned giving and corporate & foundation support. Work to develop a new pipeline of donors.
Serve as strategist to others on cultivating and securing transformational gifts and philanthropic investments.
Partner with the CEO, Board and staff to identify major donors, eligible foundations and corporate sponsors.
Design and implement customized cultivation strategies for each donor that will serve as a foundational communication and marketing plan for each individual within the portfolio.
Solicit contributions, cultivate and steward donors on behalf of the organization through a major gift portfolio of approximately 100, and corporate and foundation relationships.
Lead the development and execution of a comprehensive, multi-year fundraising strategy aligned with organizational priorities and growth objectives.
Working with the CEO and Board of Directors, participate in establishing and approval of a capital campaign goal and implementation plan.
Assist with campaign volunteer engagement including recruiting and stewarding Campaign Cabinet members; lead regular Campaign Cabinet and steering committee meetings; and conduct proactive follow-up.
Develop, refine and update the Campaign Case for Support as needed.
Create a depth chart to solicit and secure lead gifts.
Implement an annual Planned Giving strategy, working closely with planned giving professionals and others to increase the number of planned gifts members reported each year.
Collaborate with staff and volunteers to coordinate cultivation events and other activities for donors/prospective donors.
Work closely with the Director of Marketing & Communications to ensure proper coordination and integration of development in CuriOdyssey communications, collateral and other marketing efforts.
Design, implement and evaluate development budgets (income and expense) and activities which support organizational growth and fiscal soundness; combines development resources to achieve the greatest return on investment.
Attend and work closely with the Board of Directors Development Committee; provide staff support to the committee, ensuring the committee chair is successful and effective. When needed, attend and present updates to the Board of Directors and the Finance Committee.
Manage development department, including the selection, integration and growth of department to ensure employee productivity and satisfaction. Encourage open communication, proactive conflict resolution, peer support, coaching, staff development and cross department collaboration.
Define metrics and measurements quantifying performance against goals.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Minimum of 10-plus years of significant nonprofit fundraising experience and proven track record of raising more than $4 million annually.
Seven-plus years of experience in major donor cultivation, solicitation and moves management. Proven track record of building donor relationships and closing gifts in the five- six- and seven-figure range.
Direct experience in capital campaigns, special events, direct response, major gifts, planned giving, grants and corporate giving.
Capital campaign experience is required for the success of this individual. Experience in securing six- and seven-figure capital campaign gifts is a plus.
A strong knowledge of the charitable giving community in the Bay Area is helpful.
Experience working with volunteer fundraisers to successfully close major gifts among their networks.
A proven track record in creating new fundraising opportunities and reinvigorating existing programs.
Excellent interpersonal and communications skills with both internal and external constituencies, as well as written and verbal required. Proven experience in telling the story of an organization and its effectiveness. Excels at articulating organization goals, outcomes, objectives, and evaluation strategies to donors. Adept at crafting compelling and high-quality proposals, reports, solicitation letters and donor correspondence.
The ideal candidate is passionate about expanding equitable access to science learning experiences and understands how philanthropy can advance STEM education and community engagement.
Exceptionally strong strategic thinking, analytical and prospect research skills, and goal orientation are essential.
Ability to maintain highest levels of confidentiality with donor records and fund development information.
Demonstrated ability to model excellent customer service and be seen as a mentor to others in providing excellent customer service.
Must be able to effectively coordinate multiple time-sensitive projects and meet critical deadlines.
Demonstrates an ability to work independently and with individuals, groups and committees
Proven track record of managing, motivating and developing the full potential of a talented development staff.
Works well under pressure in a demanding, fast paced work environment.
Willingness to work a flexible schedule including evenings and occasional weekends.
Experience in Raiser’s Edge, Salesforce or similar donor database preferred.
Museum/zoo/aquarium/cultural institution experience is a plus, as well as organizations that have a membership function.

PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS:

The Senior Director of Development should embody the following personal characteristics:
A deep commitment to the goals and mission of CuriOdyssey.
Passion for science education, experiential learning, and expanding equitable access to STEM opportunities for children and families.
A personable, flexible, diplomatic, and respectful demeanor.
High ethical standards and a commitment to transparency.
Proven ability to serve as a team player, mentor, and leader to motivate and inspire staff and colleagues.
A well-organized and focused individual who is capable of and interested in increasing the effectiveness of the development team.

EDUCATION:
A bachelor’s degree is preferred. Certification such as CFRE (Certified Fund-Raising Executive) is a plus.

CONTACT:

Scott E. Miller
Scott Miller Executive Search
3041 Baker Street
San Francisco, CA 94123

Overview

University Relations builds Santa Clara University’s excellence and character by strengthening relations with alumni, parents, and friends of the University, raising public awareness, and increasing private philanthropy, which supports the University’s growth and reputation.

With 20 NCAA Division I sports, Athletics is an integral part of SCU's 2020 Strategic Plan and is a campaign priority. Fundraising efforts are focused on building a nationally prominent athletics program that dramatically enhances awareness of Santa Clara University, drives school spirit and alumni pride to new levels. There is also a focus on providing student-athletes with a meaningful, challenging, and rewarding academic and athletics experience.

POSITION PURPOSE

Reporting to the Senior Associate Athletics Director for Development (SAAD), the Senior Director of Development and Athletics Initiatives (SDD) plays a critical role in Santa Clara University's efforts to secure resources for its strategic funding priorities and for one of the campaign’s priorities – Athletics.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Lead the development of engagement and solicitation strategies for qualified major gift prospects (between $100,000 and $5,000,000), and oversee the implementation and personally drive the execution of said strategies.
Work closely with the Director of Athletics and the Senior Associate Athletics Director for Development to increase philanthropic support to identified Athletics funding priorities.
Collaborate with other development officers and directors of external relations, academic leaders, program directors and other University administrators, and volunteers to develop multi-interest proposals and promote organized and strategic outreach.
Develop and implement a comprehensive prospecting plan for University alumni and friends, including identification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of major gift donors, specifically for athletics.
Aggressively identify and formally qualify new prospects and existing donors through personal visits, phone calls, correspondence, events and University activities to meet fundraising objectives.
Manage a portfolio of current and new/discovery prospects, seeking to grow the pool of engaged alumni, parents, friends and corporate partners.
Incorporate planned giving alternatives as necessary and appropriate. Coordinate planned giving requests.
Meet dollar and activity metrics as set with the SAAD.
Interact with deans, directors and/or University administrators in the form of fundraising strategy development, meeting and event attendance and written briefings as they pertain to assigned prospects and prospect development.
Engage prospects and donors through athletics event invitations and attendance.
Produce well-written, accurate, and timely follow-up and related correspondence such as comprehensive proposals, related budgets, contact reports, cover and thank you letters, e-mails, reports, and briefings in support of cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding assigned prospects.

jobs.description:
We're building something new at Associated. Most organizations approach IT operations by creating separate operations centers for everything: network ops, cyber ops, infrastructure ops, cloud ops, 24-7 service desk…you get the idea. The result is many teams, many platforms, many approaches, and no one able to see the full picture of the enterprise.

We’re throwing that playbook away. We’re going to do what’s never been done before. We're going to build one unified technology operations center —a single control room for all Associated’s technology.

And we need you to lead the effort.

Associated Electric operates one of the most technologically sophisticated electric systems in the country for our members. Two data centers. Cloud platforms. Modern enterprise applications. AI in the hands of our employees. Hundreds of critical technology systems supporting 24-7 generation, transmission, and energy trading along with many other business functions. We’ve even built two operations centers for cyber and physical security, with our cyber operations center providing managed services to over 50 member cooperatives.

Our foundation is strong and ready to be taken to the next level through your transformation of our IT operations. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, you will form our new Technology Operations function, responsible for the reliability and performance of the technology of Associated, the continuity of business functions, and the productivity of our users.

This will be a tough problem to solve. Control rooms rely on control systems, but there is no commercial product on the market that we can deploy to be the control system for enterprise technology. Every product on the market sees just a small picture: network, hosting, applications, devices. Therefore, in addition to building the operations functions, you must build something that doesn't exist anywhere else—the platform it all runs on.

You won’t be starting from scratch. Associated’s CIO sponsored a cross-functional team that has spent the past nine months forming the vision for TechOps. They validated a minimum-viable business model, built the business case, and secured initial funding. We’re now set to form the TechOps organization itself with the two existing operations centers, additional support and engineering talent moving onto this team, and many of the people who built this vision in the first place. All that remains is you to lead it.

Here’s what you'll do:

Form Technology Operations:
Bring cyber operations and physical security operations together for the first time, and fuse them with platform, product, and workforce technology support into one organization with a shared mission and culture. Help some already great teams become one great organization.
Run the Operation:
Lead operations from day one so nothing pauses while you build, then grow the operation as you onboard systems. Ensure the business can trust TechOps when our grid control center or trading floor technology degrades at 3 a.m. — or when SharePoint goes down and hundreds of employees face losing a morning of productivity. Make TechOps the organization that handles an issue, an incident, or a genuine crisis with the same steadiness.
Define the Operating Model:
Define how the work happens across teams that have never worked as one — tiers and escalation, handoffs between protection and business operations, what the central floor handles versus field response at our locations, and the service definitions the business can depend on. Create one model from many.
Build the Control System:
Own the platform that powers Technology Operations: vision, roadmap, funding, and long-term evolution. Your organization builds the pipelines, alarms, and dashboards that let you understand the health of the enterprise in real time—and the AI-infused playbooks and automation that power response and recovery.
Onboard the Enterprise
: Hundreds of systems don't arrive under monitoring at once. Build the intake path — consulting services to help product teams instrument their systems, define ownership, thresholds, and runbooks — and ensure correct onboarding priority. Every system onboarded makes the picture more complete.
Expand the Services:
Grow beyond monitoring and response into what the business needs next — enterprise business continuity, disaster recovery, operational readiness, proactive health and capacity management, and coordination with the technology partners our operations depend on. jobs.title: Deputy Director of Capital Program Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
At the MBTA, we envision a thriving region enabled by a best-in-class transit system. Our mission is to serve the public by providing safe, reliable, and accessible transportation. MBTA’s core values are built around safety, service, equity, sustainability, culture, and accessibility, and each employee that works for the MBTA performs their roles based on our vision, mission, and values. This includes attendance, participation, and contribution in local safety committee meetings as needed.

Job Summary

The Deputy Director of Capital Program Planning and Analysis will help lead the development of the MBTA’s five-year capital plan through data analysis, engagement with internal and external stakeholders, and the development of decision-support tools. Working with MBTA executive leadership, the Deputy Chief of Capital Strategy, and the Senior Director of Capital Program Planning, the Deputy Director of Capital Program Planning will help create a fiscally constrained five-year capital plan that will translate the vision and goals set by the Governor, Secretary, MBTA Board of Directors, and General Manager into an achievable portfolio of tangible capital programs and projects.

The Deputy Director, working with other members of the Capital Program Planning team, will develop, implement, and monitor the process of developing the MBTA’s five-year Capital Investment Plan (CIP). The Deputy Director will also oversee processes related to project implementation, including processing project funding changes and performing ongoing analyses of capital project performance. In partnership with stakeholders across the Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) and MBTA organizations, including Deputy Chiefs, Directors, and Project Managers, the Deputy Director will be responsible for conducting quantitative analyses and developing related insights for internal decision-making and public presentations or communication related to the capital program.

Duties & Responsibilities

Lead the development of the MBTA’s $10.3B five-year Capital Investment Plan (CIP) in close collaboration with the Capital Program Planning Team, MBTA Chiefs and Deputy Chiefs, Operations leadership, asset owners, project directors and managers, and individuals at other State agencies such as MassDOT and the Executive Office of Administration and Finance.
Manage conversations in a high-pressure environment with agency leadership, municipal elected and local officials, federal partners in United States Department of Transportation (USDOT), Federal Transit Administration (FTA), Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) and Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), state partners, and staff at the various municipal planning agencies through which federal funding is allocated.
Develop and manage processes for identifying, reviewing, evaluating, and prioritizing potential capital projects for funding as part of the annual CIP update.
Engage with MBTA subject matter experts, including the Asset Management, Safety, Environmental, Security, and Systemwide Accessibility departments, to evaluate capital project requests.
Create and oversee processes to assist with implementation of the Capital Program throughout the fiscal year. Proactively identify project budget risks and monitor capital project performance to address funding needs that arise in-between annual updates to the capital plan. Manage capital funding changes between annual CIP updates to ensure alignment with approved project budget estimates at completion, schedules, performance measures, and other milestones in close collaboration with the Capital Finance and Accounting and Project Controls departments.
Evaluate and improve upon recent process to conduct project reviews for all projects over $15M each year with agency leadership. Goal of these reviews is to ensure that projects are aligned with agency priorities and are managed well to result in on-budget outcomes. Develop strategies to bring more attention to projects that are not progressing or are not the best use of funds in a highlight constrained environment.
Working with the Senior Director of CIP Development, create a data governance and management strategy for the CIP Development team, ensuring that capital project datasets are maintained and updated to allow for ongoing analysis.
Utilize data visualization, business intelligence, and geospatial intelligence systems (GIS) tools to collect, display, and analyze project data, contributing to informed decision-making within the capital program.
Design and develop executive- and public-facing presentations, reports, and other communication materials related to the MBTA's capital program, including the annual CIP book and associated web content, which will be shared with a variety of stakeholders, including the MBTA Board of Directors, the Boston Region Metropolitan Planning Organization, the MBTA Advisory Board, and members of the general public.
Develop and implement a public outreach strategy for the annual update to the CIP in coordination with External Affairs, Public Engagement, Customer Experience, and other MBTA departments.
Oversee the management of capital project portfolios by Senior Analysts, ensuring that important project information is communicated to Capital Program Planning leadership. Engage with staff from Commonwealth, Federal, and municipal partners to ensure compliance with their processes and procedures and explore funding opportunities.
Identify and implement improvements to funding-related processes to maximize the impact of capital investment and ensure the efficient utilization of funds.
Support the development of the Capital Program Planning Department, including hiring, training, and managing staff as appropriate.
Perform all other duties and projects that may be assigned.

Additional responsibilities may include focus on one or more departments or locations. See applicable addendum for department or location specific functions.

Supervision

Directly supervise one or more Senior Analysts.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Public Administration, Business Administration, Engineering, Architecture, Urban Planning, Economics, or a related field.
Five (5) years of relevant experience in a budgeting, planning, quantitative, and/or research role.
Two (2) years of supervisory, managerial, and/or leadership experience.
Effective organizational, analytical, writing, multi-tasking, and time management skills.
Advanced skill in MS Office, including Excel and PowerPoint.
